title: FinTech Inference Objection Snippets — Pocket WIP
body:
Purpose and audience:
- Short pocket reference for SEs and AEs working fintech/regulated customers (payments, neobanks, trading infra, lending platforms).
- Focus: fast objection handling when customers raise concerns about latency, auditability, data residency, encryption/KMS, model hallucinations, and procurement.

Overview / How to use:
- These are micro-snippets — 15–40s spoken answers + single-sentence email follow-ups.
- Pick the closest objection, use the spoken snippet in call, send the follow-up line as an email / slack note and attach the linked tech brief.
- If the objection needs escalation, follow the escalation checklist at the bottom.

Sections in this doc (quick nav):
- Top 8 objections and one-line rebuttals
- 30–40s spoken scripts for field use
- Email follow-ups (copy/paste)
- Short technical differentiation bullets for platform architects
- Risk & compliance quick facts (for security review kickoff)
- Pilot checklist — what to ask / what to deliver in first 30 days
- Open questions / things to resolve with product/research

Top 8 objections (one-liners):
1) "We can’t send PII to a hosted API." -> "We offer Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) + customer-managed KMS so your tokens and logs remain inside your network."
2) "Latency for live trading is too high." -> "We have latency-optimized model profiles, continuous batching controls, and Dedicated pools with SLOs — we’ll validate on a replay of your 99th-percentile traces."
3) "We need full audit trail / explainability." -> "Console-grade tracing + per-request metadata + KV cache replay gives an auditable sequence of inputs and model outputs; we can export logs to your SIEM/S3 and attach request IDs for reconstructions."
4) "How do you prevent hallucinations in regulation-sensitive flows?" -> "Combine constrained output schemas, function-calling for canonical sources, and model-selection policies; we also run prompt/regression evals tied to your golden prompt set."
5) "Costs will explode at scale." -> "Dedicated + caching + quantized model variants reduce unit cost; Optimize recommendations give workload-specific batching and cache policies to control spend."
6) "We need encryption keys under our control." -> "We support external KMS/HSM integrations for both Private and Dedicated setups — you control key rotation and access logs."
7) "Vendor lock-in worry." -> "Same API across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments; you can pin model versions and export configurations — we focus on portability."
8) "Procurement/enterprise contracting is too slow." -> "We have standard SOW templates for pilots and a dedicated GTM legal contact for regulated customers; propose a minimal-risk pilot clause (45 days)."

Spoken scripts (30–40s) — pick-and-read style:
- Latency: "Totally valid. For trading-type SLOs we typically recommend a Dedicated pool with pre-warmed workers and a small burst tier. We’ll run a short replay test against a 1–2 day trace you provide, measure p50/p95/p99, and share a tuning plan. If you want, we can scope that replay as a low-cost pilot — it’s a hard number rather than a promise on faith."

- Data residency/PII: "We frequently see this with banks. We can either stand up a Private deployment in your cloud/VPC or ship an on-prem package for air-gapped rooms. Your security team keeps key control via your KMS and we ship logs directly to your S3/ELK for auditing."

- Hallucinations/regulatory content: "We don’t try to paper-over it — we lean on guardrails: model selection, constrained output schemas, and explicit function calling to authoritative services. For a pilot we build a small eval suite seeded with your examples and monitor regression metrics daily."

- Cost objection: "We’ll show you a top-line cost model for both hosted and dedicated with cache-hit sensitivity. In pilot customers often see 20–60% per-token savings by enabling prefix caching and the right batching profile for their latency needs."

Email follow-ups (copy/paste templates):
- For latency replay request: "Thanks — can you share a 24–48hr trace (anonymized) of typical requests with timestamps and sizes? We’ll run a replay against our Dedicated profile and return a p50/p95/p99 latency report plus tuning recommendations within 5 business days. — Maya"

- For security kickoff: "Appreciate the call earlier. Next steps: 1) high-level architecture diagram, 2) scope (Private vs Dedicated), 3) KMS ownership model, 4) expected log export destination. I’ll loop in our security engineer, Priya N., to schedule a deep-dive. — Maya"

Technical differentiation bullets (for architects / platform eng):
- Unified runtime across deployments so integration points are stable: same telemetry hooks, same function-calling semantics, same API signatures.
- Model variant routing: automatic fallback to lower-cost quantized variants when latency spikes or capacity constrained.
- Prefix/KV caching store: supports per-tenant policies, TTLs and invalidation hooks for live models.
- Kernel/compilation tuning: we maintain pre-synthesized kernel sets for typical transformer shapes used in finance (short seq LLMs for normalization, long seq for document ingest).

Risk & compliance quick facts (to hand to security):
- Data plane: customer traffic can stay on-prem or in your VPC; hosted-only flows do not persist raw inputs beyond 7 days unless configured.
- Keys: external KMS supported; key rotation and usage logs available to customers.
- Audit: request ids, console traces, and model checksum records exportable for regulatory review.
- Certifications: GA roadmap for SOC2 type II and ISO27001; existing customers in payments have completed custom audits. (Follow-up: confirm current status with Security team before sending externally)

Pilot checklist (first 30 days) — minimal-scope pilot recommended for fintech:
1) Scope alignment call (SE + Sec + infra) 
2) Provide anonymized traces + golden prompts (3–5 examples per flow)
3) Decide deployment mode: hosted-dedicated / private-VPC / on-prem
4) Define SLOs: p50/p95 latency target, cost ceiling, accuracy/precision metrics for downstream task
5) Security checklist: KMS ownership, log sink, IP allowlists
6) Deliverables: replay latency report, sample rollout config, a 3-day canary run plan, and a short monitoring dashboard for the pilot

Escalation checklist (when to involve ENG/SEC/RESEARCH):
- Engineering: if latency replay shows >2x expected tail latency or incompatibility with your custom kernels (e.g., rare ops).
- Security: if customer requires FedRAMP-like controls or strict data residency not covered by our current Private options.
- Research/Applied ML: if hallucination mitigation requires a model fine-tune or RLHF step beyond prompt engineering.

Quick rebuttal crib notes for common competitor claims:
- Competitor: "We run everything in-house so no vendor risk." -> "Agreed, but that has hidden ops cost: hardware, SRE, ongoing model hygiene. Our Dedicated/Private options let you keep equivalent control while removing the day-to-day kernel and runtime maintenance overhead."
- Competitor: "Our vendor has lower latency because it's integrated." -> "Ask them for 99th percentile traces and an apples-to-apples replay; we can do the replay and show you tail latency under realistic load patterns."

Open questions / TODOs (internal):
- Confirm current compliance status (SOC2/ISO) and update the security quick facts line. (Owner: Priya, Jira: GTM-418)
- Get an example anonymized trace format for replay (owner: Diego).
- Create a 1-slide legal-friendly pilot clause snippet to hand to procurement (owner: Connor).
- Build a one-page Data Flows diagram (slide) for fintech customers showing Hosted/Dedicated/Private differences (owner: Maya / product designer).

Notes to self:
- Keep the language punchy and risk-aware — fintech buyers want specifics, not platitudes.
- Add a short appendix with sample NDA/pilot contract language we used successfully with two beta banking customers.
- We should record a 3-minute demo video of the replay process to attach to the replay email template.

Attachables (for the SE toolkit):
- sample_anonymized_trace_schema.json (reference)
- replay-sop-checklist.md (internal SOP)
- pilot-sample-sla-45days.pdf

End of doc.
